_source: AI_LAB_UNIVERSITY.md - 'Prerequisites are expressed as capabilities, never as completed lessons.'
_rule: A student who already has the capability skips the unit. Checked by a short proof task, never a quiz. This is what makes the tree navigable rather than a queue.

capabilities.statement: You can deploy a web app to a custom domain and read its build log.
capabilities.proof_task: Deploy any app to a domain you control. Paste the build log line that shows the deploy succeeded, and the commit SHA it built.

capabilities.statement: You can recover work from git after a mistake, without deleting the repository.
capabilities.proof_task: Produce a reflog excerpt showing a commit you recovered after a bad reset.

capabilities.statement: You can explain why a value works locally and fails in production.
capabilities.proof_task: Show one environment variable configured differently in two environments, and the code path that reads it.

capabilities.statement: You can ship a page that a stranger can use without instructions.
capabilities.proof_task: Link a live page and describe the one action a user takes on it.

capabilities.statement: You can enumerate every response a third-party API can return and show your handler for each.
capabilities.proof_task: For one API you call, list its documented failure responses and link the code branch that handles each. A single try/catch is not an answer.

capabilities.statement: You can make a language model return output your parser accepts, and prove the failure rate fell.
capabilities.proof_task: Show a before/after parse-failure rate with the prompt change that caused it.

capabilities.statement: You can tell that production is broken without a user telling you.
capabilities.proof_task: Show the signal - log, alert, dashboard or scheduled check - that would surface a failure in a system you run, and when it last fired.

capabilities.statement: You can write a post-mortem a stranger could act on.
capabilities.proof_task: Submit a post-mortem in the Lab failure format for an incident you caused or observed.

capabilities.statement: You can state a measured claim and attach the data behind it.
capabilities.proof_task: Publish a claim, its dataset, its sample size and at least one limitation. A claim with no stated limitation is returned.

capabilities.statement: You can state what observation would have proved you wrong.
capabilities.proof_task: For a claim you have made, write the observation that would falsify it.

capabilities.statement: You can show whether something you published was actually found.
capabilities.proof_task: Show impressions or citations for one page over a stated period, and say what you cannot conclude from it.
